audit_findings.title: Parent/NCI claim basis may be internally inconsistent
audit_findings.magnitude: $40.3m gross redemption value at 2025 year-end; $34.248m redeemable-NCI carrying value at 2026-06-30; OE allocation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A, capital expenditure or working-capital adjustments may inflate parent OE, while the redeemable-NCI put is an additional claim omitted from the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The total gross redemption value of the instruments was $ 40.3 million, had the options been exercised as of December 31, 2025, payable over a maximum of four years.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate that the $69.7m anchor contains NCI-owned cash flows because the OE reconciliation is missing. The omitted put claim is demonstrated: the $40.3m gross redemption value equals 2.8% of $1,435m base equity value, or about $0.42 per diluted share if deducted undiscounted. That claim alone would not reverse the base comparison with the $14.01 price, but the unallocated consolidated OE components could be larger, so overall materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace each OE component between consolidated and parent-attributable amounts, allocate subsidiary D&A, capex and working capital to permanent and redeemable NCI, obtain the latest put redemption calculation, and rerun with a consistent parent-OE basis and any remaining NCI claim deducted once.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method investments may be counted in both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.714m 2025 equity-method earnings, including $20.405m share of investee income after tax and $10.921m disposal gains; $12.688m dividends received; $157.5m bridge stakes
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings retained in the OE anchor are capitalized through forecast and terminal value while the same investments are added separately as stakes.
audit_findings.evidence: Dole’s consolidated net income includes its proportionate share of the net income or loss of equity method investments in affiliates.
audit_findings.explanation: A double count is not demonstrated because the OE reconciliation is absent, but the filed exposure is plainly capable of changing the conclusion. At the base model's computed operating-PV multiple of 14.046 times anchor OE, retaining the $20.405m recurring share of investee income would represent about $286.6m of operating value, before the separate $157.5m stake addition. The $10.921m disposal gains create a further one-off risk.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $69.7m anchor to equity-method earnings and dividends by investee; identify exactly what comprises stakes_net; then rerun either with all stake economics purged from OE and stakes retained in the bridge, or with the corresponding stakes removed from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded pension claims may require cash beyond reported pension expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $124.885m aggregate 2025 funded-status deficit; $23.1m estimated 2026 contributions and direct payments versus $15.9m in 2025; 2025 net periodic benefit cost $7.485m
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash funding or direct benefit payments exceeding pension expense reduce sustainable OE; alternatively, an unfunded pension claim may require a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: In the year ended December 31, 2025, employer contributions and direct benefit payments related to our defined benefit pension and other postretirement benefit plans amounted to $15.9 million and are estimated to be $23.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: An adjustment is not automatically required because pension expense already reduces earnings and deducting both funding and the deficit could double count. Nevertheless, the filed $124.885m deficit equals 8.7% of base equity value, or about $1.30 per diluted share, while projected 2026 cash payments are 33.1% of the $69.7m anchor. Those amounts are reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion even though the normalized incremental burden is not yet established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense, contributions, direct benefit payments and amounts already captured in OE; separate the port-related pension liability; determine legally required and normalized excess funding; then rerun using either the recurring excess cash burden in OE or the residual unfunded claim in the bridge, without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The Shell cleanup judgment may be an unmodeled claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: historical judgment exposure $133.3m less $26.7m attorney-fee offset = $106.6m; 2026 first-half combined legal and restructuring charge $23.054m; settlement and insurance amounts unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A settlement payment not already paid, accrued net of recovery, or reflected in normalized OE is a one-time claim ahead of common equity and requires a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Shell’s equitable claims related to the cleanup costs were tried and, on November 9, 2022, the jury delivered a verdict deciding that Shell properly incurred and will incur a total of $ 266.6 million in cleanup costs, and that BHC should bear 50.0 % of those costs, or $ 133.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing changes this from an open judgment to a June 2026 settlement supported mostly by legacy insurers, but it does not disclose the settlement amount, insurer funding, payment timing or the Shell-specific portion of the $23.054m charge. The historical $106.6m net judgment would equal 7.4% of base equity value, whereas the disclosed combined charge equals 1.6%; the record therefore cannot establish the remaining net exposure or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the executed settlement and insurance agreements, isolate the Shell-specific charge, confirm the June 30 accrual and any post-quarter cash payments or recoveries, and rerun the bridge for the unpaid net-of-insurance amount not already reflected in cash or OE.

audit_findings.title: The single-year anchor may retain nonrecurring disposal gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.045m filed 2025 pre-tax asset-sale gain, equal to 21.6% of the $69.7m anchor; maximum pre-tax base-value sensitivity about $211.3m or $2.19 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained disposal or insurance gain raises the single-year OE anchor and is then capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The gain on asset sales in the current year was $15.0 million and was primarily a result of the sale of actively marketed land in Hawaii in the Fresh Fruit segment, the sale of certain properties and machinery and equipment in the Diversified Fresh Produce – Americas & ROW segment and sale of certain properties in the Diversified Fresh Produce – EMEA segment.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention is not demonstrated because the OE adjustment schedule is missing. Materiality is nevertheless clear: the filed asset-sale gain is more than one-fifth of anchor OE, and capitalizing the entire pre-tax amount at the model's computed base operating-PV multiple would add about $211.3m. The exact correction depends on taxes and amounts already removed, while insurance proceeds and equity-investment disposal gains create additional unquantified exposure.
audit_findings.action: Produce the complete OE reconciliation for asset-sale gains, insurance proceeds, equity-investment disposal gains, restructuring and legal costs; remove genuine one-offs, retain recurring operating costs, and rerun all scenarios using the corrected after-tax anchor.

audit_findings.title: The Ecuador port transaction may invalidate the null perimeter ruling
audit_findings.magnitude: $180.0m closing cash proceeds; approximately $95.0m expected cumulative net cash proceeds; approximately $10.0m required facility capex; port OE and replacement service costs unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge must recognize post-June closing cash and transaction payments, while OE must exclude the sold port operations and include replacement terminal-service costs and associated capital needs.
audit_findings.evidence: The Port Transaction is expected to close in 2026 at a net gain.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the latest filing states that the port disposal closed on July 1, 2026, before the September 6 valuation date, yet the valuation records a null perimeter and uses the June 30 bridge. The direction is mixed because omitted net proceeds understate value, while retaining port earnings or omitting replacement costs overstates value. The approximately $95m cumulative net proceeds equal 6.6% of base equity value, and the required $10m capex adds further material adjustment, although the exact post-June bridge movement is not disclosed.
audit_findings.action: Roll the bridge forward from June 30 through September 6 using actual closing receipts, taxes, fees, cash transferred and debt movements; remove historical port OE, add arm's-length terminal fees and the approximately $10m capex, incorporate the Greenfood acquisition if applicable, and rerun all scenarios with the corrected perimeter exactly once.
